what: Quick-return mechanism. A crank-and-slotted-lever quick-return mechanism, the drive of a metal shaping machine. Motor A turns a 16 mm crank about a fixed bearing 56 mm from the lever’s pivot. The crank pin drives a sliding block inside a slotted, rocking housing, so the housing swings back and forth (about 33.6° in total) instead of turning round. A 64 mm connecting rod, attached 112 mm from the lever pivot, pushes a guided ram along a straight line; the ram stroke is about 66.2 mm. The motor turns at a constant speed, yet one ram stroke takes longer than the other. The program runs three crank turns forward and three back at 30°/s, then the same at 60°/s, with 3 s holds in between. A crank and slotted lever turn steady motor rotation into a slow working stroke and a quick return. The geometry sets the ratio: the ram takes 213.6° of crank rotation one way and 146.4° the other, 1.459 : 1, and reversing the crank swaps the slow side.
try: Reset, then Run. In stage 1 (30°/s), time the ram’s two strokes: about 4.9 s one way and 7.1 s the other.
Stage 2 turns the crank backwards. Predict before watching: which ram direction is slow now?
Stages 3–4 double the speed. Both strokes take half as long (about 2.4 s and 3.6 s), but their ratio stays the same: it comes from geometry, not from speed.
Watch the rocking housing. At the two moments it reverses, the crank pin is sliding along the slot and the ram stands still for an instant.
why: The lever reverses whenever the crank pin moves along the slot instead of across it; for a slot through the lever pivot this happens when the crank is at right angles to the lever. These two crank positions divide the crank circle unequally. For a centred slot the short arc is 180° − 2·asin(r/d) and the long arc 180° + 2·asin(r/d); with r = 16 mm and d = 56 mm that is 146.8° and 213.2°, a ratio of 1.452. In Vesper the slot line is offset 8 mm from the lever pivot, which moves the reversals to crank angles of 25.4° and 171.8°: one stroke takes 146.4° of crank rotation, the other 213.6°, a time ratio of 1.459. Because the crank speed is constant, time is proportional to crank angle. In a shaper the slow stroke cuts and the fast stroke is the idle return.
matters: Shaping and slotting machines cut on one stroke only. A quick return saves time on the idle stroke without a gearbox or any speed control. The ratio is fixed by the crank radius and the pivot distance: a crank closer in length to the pivot distance gives a larger swing and a stronger quick return, but also a faster, harsher return. Quickstroke gets a smaller quick-return effect from an offset slider-crank.
question: When the crank runs backwards, which ram stroke becomes slow, and does the time ratio change?
answer: The directions swap. The stroke that was the fast return becomes the slow one, because the crank now covers the 146.4° arc while the ram travels the other way. The ratio stays 213.6°/146.4° ≈ 1.459 in both directions and at both speeds, because it depends only on where the two reversal positions divide the crank circle.
further: Use the centred-slot formula with r = 16 mm and d = 56 mm, then explain why the model’s 1.459 differs slightly from 1.452: the 8 mm offset of the slot.

Whitworth’s quick return uses the same slot idea with the fixed pivots closer together than the crank radius, so the slotted link turns fully round. Vesper’s lever only rocks, which makes it a crank and slotted lever.
The ram speed is not constant within a stroke; it is highest near the middle of the return. Real shapers add gearing and a flywheel to carry the cutting load. Here there is no load at all.

The start position is not a stroke end: at 0° the ram is about 3 mm from its extreme. Qualified in the simulator with the reviewed law quick-return-v1 (crank 16 mm, pivot distance 56 mm, slot offset 8 mm, lever 112 mm and rod 64 mm, read from the compiled model): at every crank angle the ram stayed within 0.31 mm of its predicted position, the stroke was 66.18 mm (predicted 66.17 mm), the slow-to-quick crank-arc ratio was 1.454 to 1.458 in all four stages (predicted 1.459), and the slow direction swapped when the crank reversed. Without the crank pin the crank still turns but the ram stays put. That is a simulation result; no physical LEGO build has been tested.
formula: Centred slot: fast-stroke crank arc α = 180° − 2·asin(r/d), slow-stroke arc 360° − α, time ratio Q = (180° + 2·asin(r/d)) / (180° − 2·asin(r/d)). r = 16 mm, d = 56 mm → α ≈ 146.8°, Q ≈ 1.452. With Vesper’s 8 mm slot offset (full geometry, solved numerically): reversals at 25.38° and 171.79°, α = 146.41°, Q ≈ 1.4589; lever swing ≈ 33.6°; ram stroke ≈ 66.17 mm. Stroke times at crank speed ω: t_fast = α/ω and t_slow = (360° − α)/ω, so 4.88 s and 7.12 s at 30°/s.
